questions.stem: A cuboid has dimensions $5$ cm, $4$ cm, and $3$ cm. What is its surface area?
A cube has a side length of $6$ cm. What is its surface area?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 identical square faces: $6 \times 6^2 = 6 \times 36 = 216$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: The surface area of a prism equals:

options.text: Two cross-section areas plus the total area of all rectangular faces
The volume divided by the length
The area of the cross-section times the length
The perimeter of the cross-section times the length

questions.explanation: The surface area of a prism is the sum of the two end faces (cross-sections) plus the rectangular faces that connect them.

questions.stem: A triangular prism has a cross-section that is a right-angled triangle with legs $3$ cm and $4$ cm. The prism is $10$ cm long. The hypotenuse is $5$ cm. What is the surface area?
questions.explanation: Two triangular ends $= 2 \times \frac{1}{2}(3)(4) = 12$ cm$^2$. Three rectangular faces $= (3+4+5) \times 10 = 120$ cm$^2$. Total $= 12 + 120 = 132$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: A cube has a surface area of $150$ cm$^2$. What is the length of one side?
questions.explanation: Each face has area $\frac{150}{6} = 25$ cm$^2$. Side $= \sqrt{25} = 5$ cm.

questions.stem: An open-top cuboid box has length $8$ cm, width $5$ cm, and height $3$ cm. What is its outer surface area?
questions.explanation: Full surface area $= 2(8 \times 5 + 8 \times 3 + 5 \times 3) = 2(40+24+15) = 158$ cm$^2$. Remove the top face ($8 \times 5 = 40$): $158 - 40 = 118$ cm$^2$.
